In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: line 5440 (p. 86, sec. 4.2) reads exactly 'Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.' -- verbatim as reported. Surrounding section (pp. 85-87) is Carroll's survey of couplet-initial stress across Mixtec descriptions (Ayutla, Jicaltepec, Acatlan, Diuxi, Mixtepec..); none of the variety-specific statements concern Yucuañe. Carroll Table A.2 (the text layerpp. 276-277) confirms 'San Bartolomé Yucuañe Ycñ Yuca mvg Alta:W' is in Josserand's town sample, so the generalization nominally covers this languoid…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Pan-Mixtec generalization (Josserand's 122-town survey includes San Bartolomé Yucuañe, code 'Yuca'): primary stress falls on the first syllable (first mora) of the disyllabic/bimoraic root 'couplet', i.e. couplet-penultimate; prefixes and enclitics outside the couplet are unstressed. No description verifies this specifically for Yucuañe.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the quoted passage; Carroll notes elsewhere (pp. 92-93) that a few varieties (Ayutla, Molinos, Huajuapan, Mixtepec) are described with tone-dependent stress shifts, none of them Yucuañe.
new_statements.domain_note: second-hand and FAMILY-LEVEL: the statement is Josserand's definition of the Mixtec couplet across all varieties / for Proto-Mixtec, reported by Carroll 2015; it is not a first-hand description of Yucuañe Mixtec prosody. Domain = the couplet (root/stem foot), not the phonological word with clitics.
new_statements.identity_note: Rázuri Martínez 2016/2017 describe exactly San Bartolomé Yucuañe [mvg] = yucu1250 (pronouns only). Josserand 1983's town 'Yuca' = San Bartolomé Yucuañe (Carroll 2015 Table A.2; MixteCaSo metadata). Rázuri Martínez 2024 (also saved) is a DIFFERENT variety, Mixtec of San Pedro el Alto, mun. San Mateo Peñasco (author assigns it to ISO xtm / Glottolog sanm1293), and should not be attributed to yucu1250. English Wikipedia folds mvg into 'Ñumí Mixtec' with xtn and mie.
